questions.prompt: You deploy a new dedicated Standard Bastion host. Which subnet configuration meets its requirement?

options.text: A dedicated AzureBastionSubnet of /26 or larger.
options.explanation: Dedicated hosts require that name and minimum subnet size.
The name, dedication, and size do not meet the requirement.

options.text: GatewaySubnet shared with a VPN gateway.
options.explanation: Bastion requires its own named subnet.

options.text: AzureBastionSubnet /27 for a newly created host.
options.explanation: The legacy /27 exception does not apply to this new deployment.

questions.prompt: You use browser RDP through a dedicated Bastion host to a VM reachable by private IP. Which target-VM configuration is sufficient for the network path?

options.text: A public IP and Internet-wide RDP allow.
options.explanation: The Bastion path uses the VM's private IP.

options.text: Private-IP reachability and permitted Bastion-to-VM RDP traffic.
options.explanation: This supplies the target-side path without exposing its RDP port publicly.

options.text: No RDP listener because Bastion supplies the guest desktop service.
options.explanation: Bastion transports the connection; the guest must support RDP.

options.text: Only a DNS label on a target public IP.
options.explanation: A DNS label does not establish the Bastion-to-VM path.

questions.prompt: A user can read the VM, NIC, and Bastion resources but lacks valid guest RDP login rights. Does Azure Reader grant those rights?

options.text: Yes, Reader becomes guest administrator through Bastion.
options.explanation: Resource visibility does not grant guest administration.
The SKU does not create guest login rights.

options.text: No; resource read permissions and guest authentication are separate.
options.explanation: The user still needs a supported guest login and rights.

options.text: Yes, if the VM has no public IP.
options.explanation: Private networking does not change authentication rights.
